s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic skin lesions with slow growth, associated with bleeding after trauma, and concurrent lipolymphedema and neurological deficits
salient_findings: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
key_facts: Lesions have been growing slowly since age 24
Patient uses a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia
Lipolymphedema of the lower legs due to functional venous insufficiency
Father died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

shortlist.label: Cerebral cavernous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant and history of intracranial hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Familial cerebral cavernous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of similar conditions and detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

shortlist.label: Venous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Sonography demonstrated intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations and histopathology revealed dilated venous-like malformations

shortlist.label: Osler-Weber-Rendu syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of similar conditions and presence of multiple bluish, partially keratotic skin lesions

shortlist.label: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of lipolymphedema and venous malformations, although less likely given the specific KRIT1 variant detection

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, a family history of similar conditions, and the patient's history of intracranial hemorrhage and seizures support this diagnosis.

rejected.why: Lack of family history and genetic testing results
